title: Track deferred kernel scope: runtime effect sandbox, MIR lowering, incremental goal-state holes

comments.author: Yffe
comments.content: Items intentionally cut from the v0.1 kernel during planning, parked here so they are not lost: (1) Runtime effect sandbox that kills fx-violating syscalls at the OS boundary (design 4.1) — v0.1 does compile-time fx subsumption only. (2) True MIR-level lowering (design 3/13) — v0.1 transpiles to Verus source instead. (3) Lean-style incremental goal-state holes forge goal/fill (design 5.1) — needs a research spike; v0.1 ships whole-item forge check. Revisit each when its enabling milestone lands.

comments.author: Yffe
comments.content: Scope update: item 1 (runtime effect sandbox) is now SHIPPED via #57 — forge build emits an fx-derived seccomp filter; declared effects are enforced at the syscall boundary (killed on violation), boundary/slag confined to their declared fx. The runnable-binary gate it needed was shipped as #56 (forge build). #21 now tracks only: (2) DIRECT MIR-level lowering (we transpile to Rust which rustc takes to MIR; the thesis is satisfied transitively, direct-MIR emission is an unneeded rewrite, candidate to reframe/close); (3) the incremental goal-state REPL (forge goal/fill; we do whole-item forge check).

comments.author: Yffe
comments.content: COMPLETE. Item 1 (runtime sandbox): shipped #57. Item 2 (direct MIR): RETIRED with the thesis amendment 01c36f7c (transpile-to-Verus-Rust satisfies the thesis transitively; rustc performs the MIR lowering). Item 3 (goal-state REPL): SHIPPED via #193 — forge goal/fill/edit/battery all live, the ?N holes + OpenHole gate + the 5.1 dialogue golden. Nothing remains tracked here.
